current.lab_name: Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences, University of Helsinki (Helsinki, Finland)
current.role: First author of a 2026 Drosophila study identifying Spalt-related as an mTORC1 inhibitor driven by the integrated stress response.
current.sub: Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences & Institute of Biotechnology, University of Helsinki, Finland
story: Onur Deniz was first author of a 2026 study in fruit flies. The team found that the transcription factor Spalt-related (Salr) holds back mTORC1-driven growth and fat storage in the fat body when nutrients are scarce. Salr is switched on slowly by the integrated stress response, and it works alongside FoxO rather than downstream of it. PubMed lists Deniz at the University of Helsinki.

highlights.DEN2026: First author of the study identifying Salr as an integrated-stress-response-driven brake on mTORC1 growth in Drosophila.

pubmed_affiliation: Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences, University of Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland.

studies.title: Spalt-related is an inhibitor of mTORC1-mediated growth activated by the integrated stress response
studies.finding: Transcription factor Spalt-related (Salr) is a novel mTORC1 inhibitor in Drosophila activated by the integrated stress response, restricting anabolic growth and lipid storage during nutrient stress. Salr responds to a distinct, ISR-driven cue, acting convergently with FoxO rather than downstream of it.

story: Ville Hietakangas was last author of a 2026 study in fruit flies on how cells slow growth when food runs short. current.lab_name: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research (Basel, Switzerland)
current.role: First author of a 2003 study showing that TSC1/2 acts on Rheb to control mTOR signalling.
current.sub: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research · Basel, Switzerland
story: This 2003 cell study found that insulin switches on the small GTPase Rheb, and that the TSC1/TSC2 complex turns Rheb off by acting as its GAP (an enzyme that makes it hydrolyse GTP). Active Rheb then drives S6K1 signalling. This placed Rheb as a direct step upstream of mTOR.
Attila Garami is first author. PubMed lists him at the Friedrich Miescher Institute in Basel.

highlights.GAR2003: First author of the Rheb and TSC1/2 paper.

pubmed_affiliation: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research, Maulbeerstrasse 66, 4058 Basel, Switzerland.

studies.title: Insulin activation of Rheb, a mediator of mTOR/S6K/4E-BP signaling, is inhibited by TSC1 and 2
studies.finding: Insulin activates Rheb-GTP, inhibited by TSC1/2, positioning Rheb as the direct upstream activator of TOR.

current.lab_name: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research (Basel, Switzerland)
current.role: First author of the 2004 Nature paper on S6K1 deletion, obesity and insulin sensitivity in mice.
current.sub: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research, Basel
story: Sung Hee Um was first author of the Atlas study UMX2004 in Nature. In mice, deleting S6K1, a kinase downstream of mTORC1, protected against obesity that comes with age or a rich diet. The mice also kept better insulin sensitivity. It is a mouse study. PubMed lists Um at the Friedrich Miescher Institute in Basel.

highlights.UMX2004: First author: showed that mice lacking S6K1 resist age- and diet-induced obesity and stay insulin sensitive.

pubmed_affiliation: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research, Maulbeerstrasse 66, 4058 Basel, Switzerland.

studies.title: Absence of S6K1 protects against age- and diet-induced obesity while enhancing insulin sensitivity
studies.finding: S6K1 deletion protects mice from age- and diet-induced obesity and enhances insulin sensitivity.

current.lab_name: Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center, Institutes of Biomedical Sciences, Shanghai Medical College of Fudan University (Shanghai, China)
current.role: First author of the 2018 cryo-EM structure of human mTOR complex 2.
current.sub: Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center, Institutes of Biomedical Sciences, Shanghai Medical College
story: Xizi Chen was first author of a 2018 paper in Cell Research. PubMed lists the author at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center and at other Fudan University units in Shanghai.

The team used cryo-electron microscopy to work out the 3D shape of human mTORC2 at 4.9 angstrom resolution. The structure showed how the Rictor and mSin1 subunits sit around mTOR and block rapamycin from binding, which explains why mTORC2 is insensitive to rapamycin. This was a structural study of purified protein.

highlights.CHE2018: First author of the cryo-EM study of human mTORC2 that explained its rapamycin insensitivity.

pubmed_affiliation: Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center, Institutes of Biomedical Sciences, Shanghai Medical College of Fudan University, Shanghai, 200032, China.

studies.title: Cryo-EM structure of human mTOR complex 2
studies.finding: Cryo-EM structure of human mTORC2 defines its subunit organization and substrate access.

current.lab_name: Gene Expression Analysis Laboratory (London, England, United Kingdom)
current.role: First author of a 2008 study showing that mTORC1 controls SREBP and lipid synthesis downstream of Akt.
current.sub: Gene Expression Analysis Laboratory · London, UK
story: In cells and in fruit flies, Akt-driven lipid synthesis needed mTORC1. Rapamycin stopped the mature form of the transcription factor SREBP1 from building up in the nucleus and lowered its target genes. Silencing SREBP blocked Akt-driven fat synthesis and reduced cell size. Porstmann is the first of nine authors, and PubMed lists the Gene Expression Analysis Laboratory in London without naming a larger institution.

highlights.POR2008: First of nine authors on the study showing that mTORC1 regulates SREBP and lipogenesis in Akt-dependent growth.

pubmed_affiliation: Gene Expression Analysis Laboratory, 44 Lincoln's Inn Fields, London WC2A 3PX, UK.

studies.title: SREBP activity is regulated by mTORC1 and contributes to Akt-dependent cell growth
studies.finding: mTORC1 activates SREBP to drive lipogenesis supporting Akt-dependent cell growth.

current.lab_name: German Cancer Research Center, DKFZ (Heidelberg, Germany)
current.role: Middle-listed co-author of two Atlas studies, on G3BP proteins and the TSC complex and on malonyl-CoA as an mTORC1 inhibitor.
current.sub: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) · Heidelberg, Germany
story: A 2021 study found that G3BP1 and G3BP2, proteins best known from stress granules, also hold the TSC complex on the lysosome. Without them, mTORC1 reacts too strongly to amino acids and insulin. A 2023 study showed that malonyl-CoA, a molecule made during fatty acid synthesis, binds the catalytic pocket of mTOR and blocks it, linking fat production to mTORC1 activity.
Figlia is a middle author on both papers. PubMed lists the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg on both.

highlights.PRE2021: Middle author on the paper showing that G3BPs tether the TSC complex to lysosomes and restrain mTORC1.
highlights.NIC2023: Middle author on the paper identifying malonyl-CoA as an ATP-competitive mTORC1 inhibitor.

pubmed_affiliation: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), Heidelberg, Germany.

studies.title: G3BPs tether the TSC complex to lysosomes and suppress mTORC1 signaling
studies.finding: Adds a physical brake upstream of mTORC1. G3BP1 and G3BP2, known until then as core stress-granule proteins, also sit on the cytoplasmic face of the lysosome and are what holds the TSC complex there; without them TSC cannot reach its target and mTORC1 becomes over-responsive to amino acids and insulin. Loss of G3BP1 reproduces TSC-like hyperactivity phenotypes: faster mTORC1-driven motility in breast cancer cells, with low G3BP1 correlating with worse patient outcome, and disturbed neuronal development in zebrafish. Relevant to the Atlas because it is a lysosomal tethering step that the canonical Rheb/TSC diagram does not show.

studies.title: Malonyl-CoA is a conserved endogenous ATP-competitive mTORC1 inhibitor
studies.finding: Malonyl-CoA, an intermediate of fatty-acid biosynthesis, binds the mTOR catalytic pocket directly and acts as a conserved ATP-competitive inhibitor of mTORC1; when fatty acid synthase is downregulated, rising malonyl-CoA feeds back to dampen mTORC1 activity, linking lipogenic capacity to overall biosynthetic output.

current.lab_name: German Mouse Clinic, Institute of Experimental Genetics, Helmholtz Zentrum München (Neuherberg, Germany)
current.role: Middle (co-)author of 2 Atlas studies (EIS2016, NEF2013).
current.sub: German Mouse Clinic · Helmholtz Zentrum München · Neuherberg, Germany
story: The Atlas lists 2 studies with Johannes Beckers as a middle author. EIS2016 reports oral spermidine extending lifespan in mice, reducing heart enlargement and keeping heart relaxation normal, with the benefit lost in mice whose heart muscle cells lack the autophagy gene Atg5. NEF2013 reports rapamycin extending lifespan in mice while changing only a few classic ageing traits.

The 2013 rapamycin paper lists no affiliation for this author. A later paper from the same mouse-phenotyping group (2020) lists Johannes Beckers at the German Mouse Clinic, Helmholtz Zentrum München, with many of the same co-authors, and the 2016 spermidine record gives the same place. PubMed shows the role of the author only as a place in the author list, so no more is claimed here.

highlights.EIS2016: Co-author of the study on spermidine; listed in a middle position of the author list.
highlights.NEF2013: Co-author of the study on rapamycin ageing screen; listed in a middle position of the author list.

pubmed_affiliation: German Mouse Clinic, Institute of Experimental Genetics, Helmholtz Zentrum München, Neuherberg, Germany

studies.title: Cardioprotection and lifespan extension by the natural polyamine spermidine
studies.finding: The mammalian follow-up to EIS2009 and the reason the spermidine branch matters for human health claims: oral spermidine extends mouse lifespan, reduces cardiac hypertrophy and preserves diastolic function, and the protection disappears in mice whose cardiomyocytes lack Atg5, which makes autophagy necessary rather than merely correlated. Boundary: the human part is a dietary questionnaire correlated with blood pressure and cardiovascular incidence, so it is observational and does not carry the causal claim the mouse data carry.

studies.title: Rapamycin extends murine lifespan but has limited effects on aging
studies.finding: Rapamycin extends murine lifespan but has only limited effects on classic aging phenotypes.

current.role: First author of a 2013 mouse study showing that extra Atg5 raises autophagy and lifespan.
current.sub: School of Biological Sciences/Bio-MAX Institute · Seoul National University, Korea
story: Mice engineered to carry extra copies of the autophagy gene Atg5 lived about 17 percent longer at the median. They were leaner and more sensitive to insulin, and cells from them resisted oxidative damage better. Pyo is the first of eight authors, and PubMed lists the Global Research Laboratory at Seoul National University.

highlights.PYO2013: First of eight authors on the mouse study of Atg5 overexpression and lifespan.

pubmed_affiliation: Global Research Laboratory, School of Biological Sciences/Bio-MAX Institute, Seoul National University, Seoul 151-747, Korea.

studies.title: Overexpression of Atg5 in mice activates autophagy and extends lifespan
studies.finding: Mice engineered with extra copies of the autophagy gene Atg5 lived 17% longer and were leaner and more insulin-sensitive.

current.role: First author of the Atlas study BCH2026 (chloroquine and rapamycin fatty liver).
current.sub: Goodman Cancer Institute, McGill University, Montreal, Quebec, Canada
story: In BCH2026 (2026), Wafa B'chir is the first author; the paper is a mouse study showing that chloroquine reduces the fatty liver caused by rapamycin, and that this depends on the nuclear receptor ERR-alpha. pubmed_affiliation: Goodman Cancer Institute, McGill University, Montreal, Quebec, Canada

studies.title: Rapamycin-induced fatty liver in mice is attenuated by chloroquine co-treatment in an ERRα-dependent manner
studies.finding: Chloroquine co-treatment attenuates rapamycin-induced hepatic steatosis (a known mTORC1-inhibitor side effect) in mice, and this rescue depends on the nuclear receptor ERRα; RNA-seq shows chloroquine reverses rapamycin-driven upregulation of lipid-metabolism genes, with ERRα identified as a top transcriptional regulator of the effect.

current.role: First author of a 2026 mouse study of melittin in psoriasis-like skin inflammation.
current.sub: Health Holding Company, Aseer Health Cluster, Saudi Ministry of Health · Abha, Saudi Arabia
story: This 2026 mouse study tested melittin, the main component of bee venom, in imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like dermatitis. At the higher dose, melittin cut the clinical severity score by 60%. It also lowered PI3K/Akt/mTOR signalling and raised markers of autophagy. This is an animal study.
Saeed Hafez is first author. PubMed lists him at the Health Holding Company, Aseer Health Cluster, Saudi Ministry of Health in Abha.

highlights.HAFEZ2026: First author of the melittin psoriasis study.

pubmed_affiliation: Health Holding Company, Aseer Health Cluster, Saudi Ministry of Health, Abha, Saudi Arabia.

studies.title: Melittin attenuates imiquimod-induced psoriatic dermatitis in mice: a role for autophagy activation via PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway suppression.
studies.finding: Melittin (bee venom, 80 mg/kg i.p.) reduces psoriatic dermatitis severity by 60% in an imiquimod mouse model by suppressing PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling and activating autophagy.

current.lab_name: Healthy Longevity Translational Research Program, Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore (Singapore)
current.role: First author of a 2024 systematic review of rapamycin and its derivatives for ageing-related changes in humans.
current.sub: Healthy Longevity Translational Research Program, National University of Singapore (PubMed affiliation, 2024)
story: Deborah J W Lee was first author of a 2024 Lancet Healthy Longevity systematic review in the Atlas (LEE2024), with two co-authors. The team searched five databases and found 18,400 papers, of which 19 studies were included. Rapamycin and related drugs improved some immune, heart and skin measures, with no clear effect on hormones, muscle or the nervous system. Infections and blood fats rose in people who already had age-related disease.

highlights.LEE2024: First author of the systematic review; PubMed lists the author at the National University of Singapore.

pubmed_affiliation: Healthy Longevity Translational Research Program, Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore, Singapore.

studies.title: Targeting ageing with rapamycin and its derivatives in humans: a systematic review
studies.finding: Described by its authors as the first systematic review of rapamycin/rapalogs in humans for aging. Screened 18,400 articles, included 19 studies. Found improvements in immune, cardiovascular, and skin (integumentary) parameters; NO significant effect on endocrine, muscular, or neurological systems. No serious adverse events in healthy people, but more infections and raised cholesterol/triglycerides in people with age-related disease. This is the highest-tier human-evidence summary in the whole Atlas - it aggregates many individual human studies rather than reporting one.

current.lab_name: Heidelberg University (Heidelberg, Germany)
current.role: First author of a 2026 Blood study on IDH3, citrate and venetoclax resistance in acute myeloid leukemia.
current.sub: Heidelberg University · Heidelberg, Germany
story: Aykut Demir is first author of a 2026 paper in Blood. The work covers leukemic stem cells from acute myeloid leukemia, studied in cells, organoids and mice. Losing IDH3A, an enzyme of the TCA cycle, raised citrate and caused an energy crisis. That activated AMPK and lowered mTORC1 activity and protein production, which made the cells more sensitive to the drug venetoclax. PubMed lists him at Heidelberg University.

highlights.DEM2026: First author of the study linking IDH3A, citrate, AMPK and mTORC1 to venetoclax sensitivity in AML stem cells.

pubmed_affiliation: Heidelberg University, Heidelberg, Germany.

studies.title: IDH3 regulates citrate homeostasis to control metabolic fitness and venetoclax resistance of AML stem cells
studies.finding: IDH3A loss in AML leukemic stem cells reduces TCA cycle flux and raises intracellular citrate, activating AMPK and suppressing mTORC1 (lowering translation), which sensitizes cells to BCL2 inhibition by venetoclax - nominating the IDH3A-citrate-AMPK-mTORC1 axis as a target to overcome venetoclax/azacitidine resistance.

current.role: Last author of the 2026 study on how the pollutant EDPrB causes kidney disease through mTOR.
current.sub: Heilongjiang Key Laboratory for Laboratory Animals and Comparative Medicine · Northeast Agricultural University, Harbin, China
story: In mice and in human kidney cells grown in a dish, the pollutant EDPrB built up in the kidney and led to chronic kidney disease. The damage ran through overactive mTOR, which switched down autophagy (the cell's clean-up system) and set off inflammation and scar tissue. Giving the mice rapamycin reversed the harm, which pointed to mTOR activation as the first step in the chain. Cao is the last of five authors, and PubMed lists the affiliation as the Heilongjiang laboratory named above.

highlights.MIAO2026: Last of five authors on the mouse and cell study linking EDPrB exposure to mTOR-driven kidney disease.

current.lab_name: Hospital de Amor Nossa Senhora (Barretos, Brazil)
current.role: First author of a meta-analysis of everolimus in heart transplant recipients.
current.sub: Hospital de Amor Nossa Senhora, Barretos
story: Sofia Helena Vitte was first author of the Atlas study VITTE2026 in JHLT Open. The meta-analysis pooled 60 studies with 1786 heart transplant recipients. Everolimus-based treatment reduced the progression of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (relative risk about 0.57) and kept kidney function better when calcineurin inhibitors were reduced. Overall mortality was unchanged, and adverse events and treatment stops were more common. PubMed lists Vitte at the Hospital de Amor Nossa Senhora in Barretos, Brazil.

highlights.VITTE2026: First author: led the meta-analysis of everolimus in heart transplant recipients.

pubmed_affiliation: Hospital de Amor Nossa Senhora, Barretos, Brazil.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of everolimus in heart transplant recipients: A meta-analysis
studies.finding: Meta-analysis of 60 studies (1786 heart transplant recipients): everolimus-based immunosuppression reduced cardiac allograft vasculopathy progression on IVUS (RR ~0.57) and preserved renal function (eGFR +10-15 mL/min) when combined with calcineurin-inhibitor minimisation, with neutral all-cause mortality (RR ~0.98) but more adverse events and treatment discontinuation.

current.sub: Howard Hughes Medical Institute, Janelia Research Campus
story: Rick K. Huang is a middle author on two cryo-EM papers in the Atlas on how the Rag GTPases, which pass nutrient signals to mTORC1, are regulated. PubMed lists the author at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute, Janelia Research Campus, in Virginia.

The 2018 paper gives structures of GATOR1 and of GATOR1 bound to the Rag GTPases. The 2019 paper gives the structure of the FLCN-FNIP2 complex bound to the Rags and Ragulator. Both are structures of purified human proteins, tested with biochemical assays.
